solution: Data in ascending order: \(54, 63, 66, 72, 87, 92, 98\). Here \(n = 7\) (odd), so the median is the \(\left(\frac{n+1}{2}\right)^{th} = \left(\frac{7+1}{2}\right)^{th} = 4^{th}\) observation \(= 72\). \(\therefore\) the median of the given data is \(72\).

stem: Multiply and write the answer in the simplest form: \(5\sqrt{7} \times 2\sqrt{7}\).
solution: \(5\sqrt{7} \times 2\sqrt{7} = (5 \times 2)\left(\sqrt{7} \times \sqrt{7}\right) = 10 \times 7 = 70\).

stem: If \(3x + 5y = 9\) and \(5x + 3y = 7\), then find the value of \(x + y\).
Write the ratio of the second quantity to the first quantity in the reduced form: \(5\) dozen pens, \(120\) pens.
solution: 1st quantity \(= 120\) pens. 2nd quantity \(= 5\) dozen \(= 5 \times 12 = 60\) pens (since 1 dozen \(= 12\)). \(\therefore\) ratio of the 2nd quantity to the 1st quantity \(= 60 : 120 = \frac{60}{120} = \frac{1}{2} = 1 : 2\).

stem: Write the following polynomial in coefficient form: \(2x^{3} + x^{2} - 3x + 4\).
solution: Coefficient of \(x^{3} = 2\), coefficient of \(x^{2} = 1\), coefficient of \(x = -3\), and the constant term \(= 4\). \(\therefore\) the coefficient form of \(2x^{3} + x^{2} - 3x + 4\) is \((2, 1, -3, 4)\).

stem: For computation of income tax, which is the assessment year of the financial year \(01\text{-}04\text{-}2016\) to \(31\text{-}03\text{-}2017\)?
solution: The assessment year of the financial year \(01\text{-}04\text{-}2016\) to \(31\text{-}03\text{-}2017\) is \(01\text{-}04\text{-}2017\) to \(31\text{-}03\text{-}2018\).

Sangeeta's monthly income is Rs. \(25{,}000\). She spent \(90\%\) of her income and donated \(3\%\) for socially useful causes. How much money did she save?
solution: \(90\%\) of income \(= \frac{90}{100} \times 25000 = \text{Rs. } 22500\). \(3\%\) of income \(= \frac{3}{100} \times 25000 = \text{Rs. } 750\). Total spent \(= 22500 + 750 = \text{Rs. } 23250\). Savings \(= 25000 - 23250 = \text{Rs. } 1750\). \(\therefore\) Sangeeta saves Rs. \(1750\).

stem: In the A.P. \(2, -2, -6, -10, \ldots\) the common difference \((d)\) is:
solution: Common difference \(d = -2 - 2 = -6 - (-2) = -4\). \(\therefore\) the correct option is A.

subtopic: Standard Form of a Quadratic Equation
stem: For the quadratic equation \(x^{2} + 10x - 7 = 0\), the values of \(a, b, c\) are:
solution: Comparing \(x^{2} + 10x - 7 = 0\) with the general form \(ax^{2} + bx + c = 0\), we get \(a = 1, b = 10, c = -7\). \(\therefore\) the correct option is C.

stem: The tax levied by the Central Government for trading within a state is:
solution: The tax levied by the Central Government for trading within a state is CGST. \(\therefore\) the correct option is B.

stem: If a die is rolled, what is the probability that the number appearing on the upper face is less than \(2\)?
solution: The sample space is \(S = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}\), so \(n(S) = 6\). Let A be the event that the number is less than \(2\). Then \(A = \{1\}\), so \(n(A) = 1\). \(\therefore P(A) = \frac{n(A)}{n(S)} = \frac{1}{6}\), and the correct option is D.

stem: The first term and common difference of an A.P. are \(12\) and \(4\) respectively. If \(t_{n} = 96\), find \(n\).
solution: \(t_{n} = a + (n - 1)d = 12 + (n - 1)\times 4 = 8 + 4n\). Given \(t_{n} = 96\), so \(8 + 4n = 96 \Rightarrow 4n = 88 \Rightarrow n = 22\).

stem: If \(\begin{vmatrix} 4 & 5 \\ m & 3 \end{vmatrix} = 22\), then find the value of \(m\).
solution: \(\begin{vmatrix} 4 & 5 \\ m & 3 \end{vmatrix} = (4 \times 3) - (5 \times m) = 12 - 5m\). Given this equals \(22\): \(12 - 5m = 22 \Rightarrow 5m = -10 \Rightarrow m = -2\).

stem: Solve the following quadratic equation: \(x^{2} + 8x + 15 = 0\).
solution: \(x^{2} + 8x + 15 = 0 \Rightarrow x^{2} + 5x + 3x + 15 = 0 \Rightarrow x(x + 5) + 3(x + 5) = 0 \Rightarrow (x + 5)(x + 3) = 0 \Rightarrow x = -5\) or \(x = -3\).

subtopic: Shares — Face Value, Market Value, Brokerage
stem: Smita has invested Rs. \(12{,}000\) to purchase shares of FV Rs. \(10\) at a premium of Rs. \(2\). Find the number of shares she purchased.
solution: FV \(=\) Rs. \(10\), Premium \(=\) Rs. \(2\). \(\therefore\) MV \(=\) FV \(+\) Premium \(= 10 + 2 =\) Rs. \(12\). No. of shares \(= \frac{\text{Total investment}}{\text{MV}} = \frac{12000}{12} = 1000\) shares. \(\therefore\) the number of shares Smita purchased is \(1000\).

stem:
The following table shows the daily supply of electricity to different places in a town. To show the information by a pie diagram, find the measures of the central angles of the sectors.

| Places | Supply of electricity (Thousand units) |
|---|---|
| Roads | 4 |
| Factories | 12 |
| Shops | 6 |
| Houses | 8 |
| Total | 30 |
solution: Measure of central angle \(= \frac{\text{supply of the place}}{\text{total supply}} \times 360^{\circ}\). Roads \(= \frac{4}{30} \times 360 = 48^{\circ}\); Factories \(= \frac{12}{30} \times 360 = 144^{\circ}\); Shops \(= \frac{6}{30} \times 360 = 72^{\circ}\); Houses \(= \frac{8}{30} \times 360 = 96^{\circ}\).

stem: Two coins are tossed simultaneously. Write the sample space \(S\) and the expected outcomes of the events: Event A: to get at least one head; Event B: to get no head.
solution: \(S = \{HH, HT, TH, TT\}\), so \(n(S) = 4\). Event A (at least one head): \(A = \{HH, HT, TH\}\). Event B (no head): \(B = \{TT\}\).

stem: Find the \(19^{th}\) term of the A.P. \(7, 13, 19, 25, \ldots\)
Obtain a quadratic equation whose roots are \(-3\) and \(-7\).
solution: If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are the roots, the quadratic equation is \(x^{2} - (\alpha + \beta)x + \alpha\beta = 0\). Here \(\alpha = -3\) and \(\beta = -7\), so \(\alpha + \beta = -10\) and \(\alpha\beta = (-3)(-7) = 21\). \(\therefore x^{2} - (-10)x + 21 = 0 \Rightarrow x^{2} + 10x + 21 = 0\).

stem: Two numbers differ by \(3\). The sum of the greater number and twice the smaller number is \(15\). Find the smaller number.
solution: Let the greater number be \(x\) and the smaller number be \(y\). Then \(x - y = 3\) ...(1) and \(x + 2y = 15\) ...(2). Multiplying (1) by 2: \(2x - 2y = 6\) ...(3). Adding (2) and (3): \(3x = 21 \Rightarrow x = 7\). Substituting in (1): \(7 - y = 3 \Rightarrow y = 4\). \(\therefore\) the smaller number is \(4\).

subtopic: Sum of n Terms of an A.P.
stem: Amit saves a certain amount every month in a specific way. In the first month he saves Rs. \(200\), in the second month Rs. \(250\), in the third month Rs. \(300\) and so on. How much will be his total savings in \(17\) months?
solution: The savings \(200, 250, 300, \ldots\) form an A.P. with \(a = 200\) and \(d = 50\). \(S_{n} = \frac{n}{2}\left[2a + (n - 1)d\right]\). \(S_{17} = \frac{17}{2}\left[2(200) + (17 - 1)\times 50\right] = \frac{17}{2}(400 + 800) = \frac{17}{2}\times 1200 = 17 \times 600 = \text{Rs. } 10{,}200\). \(\therefore\) Amit's total savings in \(17\) months is Rs. \(10{,}200\).

stem: A two-digit number is to be formed using the digits \(0, 1, 2, 3\). Repetition of the digits is allowed. Find the probability that a number so formed is a prime number.
solution: Zero cannot be at the tens place (else it is not a two-digit number). \(S = \{10, 11, 12, 13, 20, 21, 22, 23, 30, 31, 32, 33\}\), so \(n(S) = 12\). Let A be the event that the number formed is prime. \(A = \{11, 13, 23, 31\}\), so \(n(A) = 4\). \(\therefore P(A) = \frac{n(A)}{n(S)} = \frac{4}{12} = \frac{1}{3}\).

stem: Smt. Malhotra purchased solar panels for the taxable value of Rs. \(85{,}000\). She sold them for Rs. \(90{,}000\). The rate of GST is \(5\%\). Find the ITC of Smt. Malhotra. What is the amount of GST payable by her?
solution: Output tax (tax collected at the sale) \(= 5\%\) of \(90000 = \frac{5}{100}\times 90000 = \text{Rs. } 4500\). Input tax (tax paid at the purchase) \(= 5\%\) of \(85000 = \frac{5}{100}\times 85000 = \text{Rs. } 4250\). \(\therefore\) Input Tax Credit (ITC) \(=\) Rs. \(4250\). GST payable \(=\) Output tax \(-\) ITC \(= 4500 - 4250 = \text{Rs. } 250\). \(\therefore\) the ITC is Rs. \(4250\) and the GST payable by Smt. Malhotra is Rs. \(250\).

stem: Solve the following simultaneous equations graphically: \(x + y = 0\); \(2x - y = 9\).
solution: For \(x + y = 0\): the points are \((0, 0), (1, -1), (-1, 1)\). For \(2x - y = 9\): the points are \((0, -9), (1, -7), (5, 1)\). On plotting both lines on the same graph, they intersect at \((3, -3)\). \(\therefore\) the solution is \((3, -3)\).

stem:
The following frequency distribution table shows the marks obtained by \(180\) students in a Mathematics examination. Find the value of \(x\). Also draw a histogram representing the above information.

| Marks | Number of Students |
|---|---|
| 0 – 10 | 25 |
| 10 – 20 | \(x\) |
| 20 – 30 | 30 |
| 30 – 40 | \(2x\) |
| 40 – 50 | 65 |
solution: The total number of students is \(180\). \(25 + x + 30 + 2x + 65 = 180 \Rightarrow 3x + 120 = 180 \Rightarrow 3x = 60 \Rightarrow x = 20\). So the frequencies are \(25, 20, 30, 40, 65\). To draw the histogram, take Marks on the X-axis and Number of students on the Y-axis, and draw rectangles on each class with heights proportional to the frequencies.

stem: Two taps together can fill a tank completely in \(3\frac{1}{13}\) minutes. The smaller tap takes \(3\) minutes more than the bigger tap to fill the tank. How much time does each tap take to fill the tank completely?
solution: The two taps together fill the tank in \(3\frac{1}{13} = \frac{40}{13}\) minutes, so the combined rate \(= \frac{13}{40}\) tank per minute. Let the bigger tap take \(t\) minutes; then the smaller tap takes \((t + 3)\) minutes. \(\frac{1}{t} + \frac{1}{t + 3} = \frac{13}{40}\). \(\Rightarrow \frac{(t + 3) + t}{t(t + 3)} = \frac{13}{40} \Rightarrow 40(2t + 3) = 13t(t + 3) \Rightarrow 80t + 120 = 13t^{2} + 39t \Rightarrow 13t^{2} - 41t - 120 = 0\). By the quadratic formula, \(t = \frac{41 \pm \sqrt{41^{2} + 4(13)(120)}}{2 \times 13} = \frac{41 \pm \sqrt{7921}}{26} = \frac{41 \pm 89}{26}\). Taking the positive root, \(t = \frac{130}{26} = 5\). \(\therefore\) the bigger tap takes \(5\) minutes and the smaller tap takes \(8\) minutes to fill the tank completely.

stem: The co-ordinates of the point of intersection of the lines \(ax + by = 9\) and \(bx + ay = 5\) is \((3, -1)\). Find the values of \(a\) and \(b\).
solution: Since \((3, -1)\) satisfies both equations: from \(ax + by = 9\), \(3a - b = 9\) ...(i); from \(bx + ay = 5\), \(3b - a = 5\) ...(ii). Multiplying (ii) by 3: \(9b - 3a = 15\) ...(iii). Adding (i) and (iii): \(8b = 24 \Rightarrow b = 3\). Substituting in (ii): \(3(3) - a = 5 \Rightarrow 9 - a = 5 \Rightarrow a = 4\). \(\therefore a = 4\) and \(b = 3\).
